semantics.businessDeployableDefinition: Long-running product processes that own Phase 1 business request, telemetry processing, or metric execution responsibility.
semantics.integrationReason: IoT connectivity and MQTT are deployment-specific integration capabilities. Backend/UI production must be able to run without a local MQTT broker or iot-service.
semantics.postgresPlacementReason: Stage 1 enables the local-postgres profile by default. Stage 2 can omit that profile and point migration, preflight and application DSNs at an external PostgreSQL endpoint without changing application topology.
semantics.clickhousePlacementReason: Stage 1 enables the local-clickhouse profile by default. Stage 2 can omit that profile and point the shared ClickHouse HTTP endpoint plus service credentials at an externally provisioned ClickHouse data plane.
semantics.redisPlacementReason: Stage 1 enables the local-redis profile by default. Stage 2 can omit that profile and point OIDC state, realtime recovery, Latest projections, Metric Latest and shared limit counters at an external Redis endpoint without changing application topology.
semantics.supportingWorkloadDefinition: Long-running application workers that coordinate or execute cross-domain operational jobs without becoming a new business-domain authority.
semantics.maintenanceReason: Maintenance executes credential-expiry scans, dead-work disposition and Tenant retirement with cross-domain operational privileges. Folding it into scheduler would violate the Scheduler coordination-only boundary; folding it into energy-api would widen the online API process privilege set.
semantics.identityReason: identity-service owns authentication credentials and OIDC only; Tenant/Site/Role/Policy authorization remains inside platform IAM.
semantics.intelligenceReason: Forecast, Optimization and FDD do not gate telemetry, control safety or the default Phase 1 runtime and are enabled only through the intelligence profile.
semantics.oneShotReason: Migration, bootstrap, administration, schema preflight and backup actions are explicit lifecycle/operations actions rather than continuously running product services.
